title: Norman Rockwell: the fun ones
museum: Various (Norman Rockwell Museum, Crystal Bridges, the Baseball Hall of Fame and private collections)
videoFormat: None: a gallery carousel following the Freedom from Want reel
caption:
You know these paintings. Most people don't know his name: Norman Rockwell.

1. The Shiner (1953). Black eye, outside the principal's office, and absolutely no regrets.
2. The Connoisseur (1962). That splatter painting? Rockwell made it himself, dripping paint like Jackson Pollock.
3. Rosie the Riveter (1943). Her pose is borrowed from Michelangelo's prophet Isaiah on the Sistine Chapel ceiling.
4. Art Critic (1955). The student is his son Jarvis. The lady in the painting is his wife, Mary.
5. The Runaway (1958). The trooper and the boy were real neighbours who posed for him.
6. Tattoo Artist (1944). Read the sailor's arm: a list of girlfriends' names, every one crossed out but the newest.
7. Soda Jerk (1953). One soda jerk, three girls, one very unimpressed dog.
8. Triple Self-Portrait (1960). Pinned to his canvas: Dürer, Rembrandt, Picasso and Van Gogh.
9. Doctor and the Doll (1929). A real check-up, for a patient made of porcelain.
10. Game Called Because of Rain (1949). Three real umpires at Ebbets Field. It now hangs in the Baseball Hall of Fame.
11. Freedom from Want (1943). The Thanksgiving painting that wasn't about Thanksgiving. It was one of his Four Freedoms.
12. New Television Set (1949). A brand-new TV antenna on a very old house.

Which one made you smile first? Save this for later.
